name: ORB trend day, hold to close
hypothesis: Large institutional parent orders on exceptional-volume days (opening-range volume 3x its 20-day norm) are worked across the whole session, so a break of the first 30-minute high on such a day keeps drifting into the close. The earlier ORB test failed because a 0.6% stop and 1.2% target made it a coin flip charged 5.5 bps a trade; this one trades rarely, holds to the close with a wide stop and a target that is rarely hit, so cost is small against the move. Written before any run. Expected to fail if breakouts on heavy-volume days mean-revert by the afternoon as liquidity providers reload, or if gross stays about zero as in the first ORB.
